title: Uruguayan Beef Empanadas
description: A traditional Uruguayan dish featuring savory beef filling wrapped in a long-fermentation dough, perfect for a weeknight dinner. The addition of mustard seeds gives it a unique flavor.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, salt, sugar, and yeast to make the dough.
Gradually add water to the dry ingredients and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Let the dough ferment in a warm place for 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
In a separate pan, heat olive oil and saute the onion until it is translucent.
Add the ground beef to the pan and cook until it is browned, breaking it up into small pieces.
Stir in the mustard seeds and cook for an additional minute.
Divide the fermented dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle and place a tablespoon of the beef filling in the center.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape and press the edges together to seal the empanada.
Brush the tops of the empanadas with olive oil and bake in a preheated oven at 375 degrees for 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
